title: Coin vs Token — the Difference
summary: A coin is the native asset of its own blockchain — Bitcoin on the Bitcoin network, Ether on Ethereum. It is used to pay that network's fees and secure it.
blocks: A coin is the native asset of its own blockchain — Bitcoin on the Bitcoin network, Ether on Ethereum. It is used to pay that network's fees and secure it.
A token is issued on top of an existing blockchain using its standards, rather than having a chain of its own. Many assets you see are tokens on Ethereum or other networks.
The distinction matters for how something works under the hood, but in a price list both simply appear as tradable assets with a market value.
